toyota_summary:
Middle East supply chain disruptions are reshaping logistics and trade flows across the region. Jetro reports that political instability is forcing companies to reassess operations, inventory placement, and routing strategies in real time. This matters because automakers source components and materials from the Middle East and route finished vehicles through regional ports. Any sustained closure or diversion of trade corridors will force costly workarounds and delay deliveries to Africa, Europe, and Asia. Watch whether the Strait of Hormuz or key ports see actual shipping halts in the next two weeks.

The EU is pressing Brussels to loosen its green steel and cement requirements in the Industrial Accelerating Act, seeking flexibility to adjust local sourcing quotas by country rather than applying uniform rules across the bloc. That softens a rule that would have forced automakers and suppliers to source exclusively from approved European mills—a cost burden many opposed. The real shift is reframing "Made in Europe" around bilateral trade deals with individual countries instead of bloc-wide content rules. This gives manufacturers more latitude to source from Turkey, the UK, and other partners without penalty.

China announced a five-year sports industry plan targeting 7 trillion yuan in sector growth by 2030, while also weighing fiscal stimulus and new industrial policies for the second half of the year. Watch China's fiscal announcement in the next month—if they unlock spending on infrastructure and manufacturing, it could lift demand for commercial vehicles and electric powertrains faster than expected.

emails.subject: Document: EU countries seek flexibility over green steel and
emails.excerpt: EU加盟国は、気候に優しい建築材料の製造を促進する法律の修正権をブリュッセルに付与するこ
emails.subject_en: Document: EU countries seek flexibility over green steel and cement quotas
emails.summary_en: EU member states are pushing to give the European Commission flexibility to revise mandatory quotas for low-carbon steel, aluminum, and cement in public works projects, citing concerns over material costs, supply security, and competitiveness against China and the U.S. The proposed amendment to the Industrial Accelerator Act would also extend EU-origin requirements to steel, previously exempt. The move reflects a broader pattern of the EU softening its green industrial policies amid competitiveness concerns.
emails.summary_ja: EU加盟国は、公共事業における低炭素鉄鋼・アルミニウム・セメントの義務的な使用割合について、欧州委員会に見直し権限を与えるよう求めている。これは、材料コストの上昇や供給の安全性、中国・米国との競争力への懸念を背景にしたもの。産業加速化法の改正案では、これまで対象外だった鉄鋼にもEU域内製造の要件を拡大する方針で、EUが競争力への懸念から環境政策を後退させる傾向の一環となっている。

emails.subject: Document: EU countries recast ‘Made in Europe’ around products,
emails.excerpt: EU政府は産業加速法の「メイド・イン・ヨーロッパ」概念を、国ではなく製品ごとの貿易協定に
emails.subject_en: Document: EU countries recast ‘Made in Europe’ around products, not countries
emails.summary_en: EU governments are refining the Industrial Accelerator Act's 'Made in Europe' provision, shifting from a broad country-based approach to a product-specific 'partner origin' system tied to existing trade and procurement agreements. The Council's compromise, which would give member states more control via implementing acts, aims to narrow the Commission's original expansive proposal that could have covered up to 80 countries. The change matters for automakers and industrial firms competing for EU public contracts and subsidies tied to local content rules.
emails.summary_ja: EU各国は、産業加速化法(IAA)の「メイド・イン・ヨーロッパ」規定を見直し、国単位の広範な枠組みから、既存の貿易・調達協定に基づく製品別の「パートナー原産地」制度への移行を進めている。理事会の妥協案は加盟国が実施法を通じてより強い決定権を持つことを目指し、最大80カ国を対象とし得た欧州委員会の当初案を絞り込む狙いがある。この変更は、EUの公共調達や補助金における現地調達要件を巡り競争する自動車メーカーや産業界にとって重要な意味を持つ。

emails.summary_en: US regulators granted Zoox a regulatory exemption to speed commercial rollout of its self-driving vehicles, while two major US automakers reported weaker Q2 bottom lines due to EV restructuring costs but raised full-year guidance. Meanwhile, Brazil's domestic auto sales jumped 18.5% year-on-year in H1, even as exports fell 21.2%, reflecting diverging trends between local demand and trade in key automotive markets.

emails.subject: EU countries drop mandatory industrial acceleration areas from IAA
emails.subject_en: EU countries drop mandatory industrial acceleration areas from IAA
emails.summary_en: The EU Council's Irish presidency has softened the Industrial Accelerator Act, making industrial acceleration zones optional rather than mandatory for member states. For automakers, a key provision survives: manufacturers can self-declare EU-origin compliance if at least 85% of vehicles assembled the prior year met the rules, offering flexibility on local content requirements. The revised text also lets national governments retain more control over permitting, foreign investment screening, and approval of partner countries for origin equivalence.
emails.summary_ja: EU理事会のアイルランド議長国は「産業加速化法」を緩和し、加盟国に義務付けていた産業加速地域の指定を任意とする方向で調整している。自動車業界にとって重要な点として、前年に組み立てた車両の85%以上がEU原産規則を満たしていれば自己申告で対応できる柔軟措置が維持された。さらに改訂案では、許認可手続きや外国投資審査、原産地同等性を認めるパートナー国の承認について、加盟国政府の権限を強める内容となっている。
